articles.title: Bills vs. Rams live updates, inactives, where to watch: DJ Moore inactive as Josh Allen, Matthew Stafford face off in potential Super Bowl LXI preview
articles.summary: The Rams and Bills will close out Week 5 on "Monday Night Football."
articles.body: The Buffalo Bills head west to close out Week 5 against the Los Angeles Rams on “Monday Night Football,” with kickoff set for 8:15 p.m. ET at SoFi Stadium.Despite a 2-2 start, the Rams remain the favorites to win Super Bowl LXI at +600 on FanDuel Sportsbook, with the 3-1 Bills not far behind at +850. Those odds tell only part of the story heading into Monday’s finale, which could very well be a preview of this season’s Super Bowl, a showdown between the last two NFL MVPs in Josh Allen (2024) and Matthew Stafford (2025).The Bills will be without one of their top receiving weapons in Week 5, with wideout DJ Moore inactive due to a shoulder injury he aggravated in last week’s loss to the New England Patriots, along with WR Joshua Palmer. The Rams, meanwhile, will have All-Pro defensive tackle Aaron Donald available after missing last week with back soreness. None of those news items should considered a positive for Allen, with the Bills already 3.5-point road underdogs Monday night.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Rams host the Bills to close out Week 5 on “Monday Night Football,” airing on ESPN.

articles.title: Dodgers vs. Brewers score, live updates: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Logan Henderson take the mound in Game 2 of NLCS
articles.summary: The Brewers took Game 1 of the NLCS with a 2-1 win over the Dodgers on Sunday.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers are back in action on Monday for Game 2 of the NLCS at American Family Field in Milwaukee, with first pitch set for 5 p.m. ET. After getting swept by the Dodgers in last year's NLCS, the Brewers came out with a 2-1 win in Game 1, with Los Angeles' offense looking vulnerable as it continues to struggle to produce hits with runners in scoring position.The Dodgers will deploy another ace Monday, following Game 1's start from Tarik Skubal with right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-9, 2.53 ERA) on the mound. Yamamoto's lone start of this postseason came in Game 3 of the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves, and he struck out 10 while giving up four hits and one earned run over seven innings.The Brewers will start right-hander Logan Henderson (11-3, 2.47 ERA) in Game 2. He most recently started Game 2 of the NLDS against the San Diego Padres, a 4-3 win thanks to some late-game heroics from outfielder Jackson Chourio. Henderson pitched five innings in that game, striking out 4 and walking 3 while allowing 2 runs (1 earned). Left-handed hitters Christian Yelich, Sal Frelick and David Hamilton are all back in the lineup in Game 2 after sitting against left-hander Skubal in Game 1. Yelich and Frelick both scored on Chourio's walk-off single in Game 2 of the NLDS.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Brewers host the Dodgers in Game 2 of the NLCS, airing on Fox.
